findings.text: blocking: the over-ceiling branch composes argv as [os.path.abspath(batch), *placement_module.own_job_prefix(...)] while own_job_prefix (reckon/crew/placement.py:459-460) already leads with the literal STEP_JOB_SCHEDULER, so the executed argv is ['/abs/sbatch', 'sbatch', '--wait', '--wrap', ...]; sbatch takes the token 'sbatch' as a positional script beside --wrap, so every >48 GB declaration fails to launch and the goal's own-job route is unreachable in practice.

blocking: own_job_prefix places the worker through 'sbatch --wait --wrap <cmd>', which writes the worker's stdout to slurm-<jobid>.out rather than to the caller's pipe, so a run placed this way leaves the supervisor only 'Submitted batch job N' and loses its stream, timing and stop path; the same composition also sets stdin_text='' at dispatch_launch.py:1149, dropping the plan's stdin.

follow-on: the ceiling test asserts argv[0] == SBATCH but never that the scheduler name appears exactly once nor that --wrap is positioned as a script body, so it stays green on the duplicated-scheduler argv and cannot redden on the blocking defect it was added to guard.

follow-on: the default bound is asserted only against placement.DEFAULT_STEP_MEMORY_GB, the same constant the code under test reads (also at :89 and :170), so both sides move together and no test fails if the default leaves 24 GB.

follow-on: the manifest's cited gates do not reconcile with what they record - the tests line states '131 passed, 1 skipped' while logs/focused-gate.log now reads '132 passed, 1 skipped' labelled revision=1315da56, and after_suite names revision 0857984c while logs/gate-head.log reads revision=808f88ea; the cause is the reviewed run's own concurrent resume rewriting those logs, not a fabricated figure, but a reader cannot confirm the recorded figure from the cited log.

follow-on: reckon/crew/summary.py is outside the node's recorded write_paths and is found by check-manifest; the change was directed by the coordinator's resume advice (make one reader the owner and have summary.py call it), so the record needs its write scope widened rather than the change reverted.
